points: Q3 2026 results will test whether the 90-day revenue estimate cuts of -35.6% were justified; a miss or reduced guidance would confirm the negative revision trend and support the short.
FY1 EPS consensus of $0.85 already embeds a -33% decline; the print will show whether management expects the full year to fall below that, putting the FY2 rebound case at risk.
FY2 EPS growth of +26.5% is the recovery thesis; Q3 commentary and guidance will reveal whether that rebound is intact or needs to be cut back.

TRIP trades at a 0.4x theme P/E discount, but if the print brings further estimate cuts the discount is likely a value trap rather than a floor; the short works if the multiple compresses alongside earnings.
ABNB, EXPE and MAR report within days of TRIP; their demand and pricing commentary will provide a read-through on whether TRIP's weakness is company-specific or sector-wide.
Reports from the Q2 call suggest management is focused on 'experiment and learn' initiatives; Q3 will reveal whether those efforts are translating into revenue or still pressuring margins.
watch: Q3 revenue vs consensus and guidance direction — further cuts support the short.
FY1 EPS guidance vs $0.85 consensus — a guide-down supports the short.
FY2 EPS estimate revisions after the print — cuts to the +26.5% growth case support the short.
Peer demand commentary from ABNB/EXPE/MAR — weaker travel trends support the short.
